nodes.name: Build Apify Query
nodes.notes: Emits one query per inventory unit. It used to read $json and scan only the first of twelve.

parameters.notes: Runs once per item. Carries each JSON-LD offer's own name and condition, then picks the offer that best matches OUR unit rather than the lowest number on the page, and records which offer won and how confident the match is. Also stores the listing's own title, the page host and a source class, so the Competitors screen can show a comparison instead of asserting one.

nodes.name: Parse AI Price
nodes.notes: Runs once per item. In all-items mode it read $json and parsed exactly one of sixteen scraped pages; .first() also mispaired the metadata. Prefers schema.org JSON-LD over the model, and takes the source from the page hostname, which always exists.

' + ($json.matchNote || '') : ($json.priceDiff < 0 ? 'UNDERCUT: competitor is AED ' + Math.abs($json.priceDiff) + ' cheaper on ' + ($json.offerName || 'an unnamed offer') + '. Consider matching, especially at ' + $json.daysInStock + ' days in stock.' : 'HOLD: we are already AED ' + $json.priceDiff + ' cheaper than ' + ($json.offerName || 'this competitor') + '.')) }}

'REJECTED' : 'SUCCESS')), lead_name: null, lead_email: null, summary: (($json.skipReason ? ('Scrape produced no usable intel for ' + ($json.model || 'a unit') + ' — ' + $json.skipReason) : ('Competitor price recorded for ' + ($json.model || 'a unit'))) + ($json.delivery ? ' | ' + $json.delivery.note : '') + (t ? '' : ' | TENANT UNRESOLVED')), logged_at: $now.toUTC().toISO(), tenant_id: t }); })() }}
